assessments.name: Involved-Leader
assessments.description: A multi-rater diagnostic inventory that dives deep into scientifically grounded and analytically proven drivers of leadership effectiveness.
assessments.instructions:
INSTRUCTIONS:

​- Think of [name] when completing this assessment. Specifically, think about how often [name] engages in the behaviors for each statement.

- Be completely honest in responding to each and every statement. Your responses will NOT be shared with anyone, only aggregated averages will be shared. This will not only benefit [name], but also the entire team that [name] leads, including you.​

- Thank you in advance!

dimensions.name: Relationships
dimensions.definition: Building relationships with, between, and among stakeholders as well as increasing harmony at work, specifically in one\'s workgroup.

dimensions.name: Servitude
dimensions.definition: Getting involved in providing yourself, time, and expertise as well as external resources to help serve others at work.

dimensions.name: Ethical
dimensions.definition: Personally and professionally following and promoting a strong ethical code across all work activities.

dimensions.name: Analytical
dimensions.definition: Uses and adheres to empirical evidence derived from appropriate analytical tools and analyses (rather than relying on intuition).

dimensions.name: Conflict
dimensions.definition: Personally involved in effectively working to overcome and resolve conflict among colleagues, whether being the mediator or active participant in conflict.

dimensions.name: Communication
dimensions.definition: Providing clear and appropriate communication, both horizontally and vertically, thereby allowing team members to complete work tasks in a highly effective manner.

dimensions.name: Rewards
dimensions.definition: Providing stakeholders personally valued recognition and rewards for strong performance and unparalleled/unique achievements.

dimensions.name: Empower
dimensions.definition: Enabling others to take ownership of their work by sharing leadership, providing job autonomy and meaningfulness to work, demonstrating confidence in performance, and facilitating goal accomplishment.

dimensions.name: Authenticity & Self-Awareness
dimensions.definition: Knowing and showing your authentic self to others at work while simultaneously knowing how you are portrayed across all work settings so to align self and other perceptions of your leadership.

dimensions.name: Change & Resilience
dimensions.definition: Understanding your leadership role in change, proactively anticipating the need for change as well as demonstrating effectiveness at leading change and a willing and-able approach to positively respond to setbacks.

assessments.name: Involved-Blockers
assessments.description: Identifies personality attributes that are preventing you from realizing your full involvement and leadership potential.
assessments.instructions:
Instructions:

In responding to each statement, think about a typical work day or work week, and rate your agreement with each statement. Please respond honestly to each question and please note, that some items might be similar to other items, this is intentional.

dimensions.name: Fear
dimensions.definition: Being too fearful to learn, try new things, or to lose face such that it prevents you from being involved to your potential. You would rather focus on showing what you can do rather than what you can’t do.

dimensions.name: Willfulness
dimensions.definition: Thick-headed and egotistical such that you typically believe you have all the answers, are a trusted expert, have more to provide than others at work, and/or are usually correct.

dimensions.name: Justification
dimensions.definition: Typically using excuses to deflect any potential blame or fault from you to other people or situations. Heavy use of rationalization to avoid blame.

dimensions.name: Victimization
dimensions.definition: Feeling that you are the one who is typically blamed when things don’t work out even though you are innocent or played no part in why things failed (or so you believe).

dimensions.name: Entitlement
dimensions.definition: A general belief that you are owed more than other people because of who you are such that you expect to receive increased and positive outcomes with minimal input on your part.

assessments.name: Involved-Me
assessments.description: A self-report version of the Involved-Leader, providing great insight into scientifically grounded, yet analytically proven drivers of leadership effectiveness.
assessments.instructions:
​Think of your own leadership style when stating your agreement or disagreement with the following statements. Select the choice that corresponds to your level of agreement for each statement.

Please keep in mind: A lot of people tend to think very highly of themselves and often times are not completely honest with themselves when completing self-assessments - this will hurt you and your leadership development. Be completely honest in responding to each and every question. It will benefit you tremendously.
